definition: When waves or pulses overlap, the resultant displacement at each point is the sum of the displacements each would cause on its own.
Two sources are coherent when they have the same frequency and a constant phase difference, which a steady interference pattern needs.
How far one oscillation is ahead of another, as a fraction of a cycle written as an angle: one cycle is $2\pi$ rad or $360^\circ$.
Waves arriving in phase add to a larger amplitude; for sources in phase it happens where the path difference is $n\lambda$.
Waves arriving in antiphase partly or fully cancel; for sources in phase it happens where the path difference is $(n + \frac{1}{2})\lambda$.
The difference between the distances two waves travel from their sources to the same point.
The evenly spaced bright and dark fringes formed when coherent light passes through two narrow slits, with fringe separation $s = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$.
